notes.1a: There were a number of very good responses with a noticeable improvement in presentation. A number of well-prepared candidates were able to gain full marks. Some candidates did not correctly adjust for the items of damaged inventory and adjustment of the opening accrual for administrative expenses was often added instead of deducted.
notes.1b: Very few candidates were able to offer more than an unclear explanation as to the meaning of reserves being maintained in their most flexible form.
notes.1c: Preparation of the ordinary share capital account produced mixed responses. Several candidates included dividends in the account, and did not separate the share premium and retained earnings segments of the issue.
notes.1d: Preparation of the statement of changes in equity was generally well done. The most common error was the inclusion of the proposed dividend that was not to be paid until after the year-end. Candidates must be made aware that the statement of changes in equity is part of the published financial statements and as such, correct labelling is important.
notes.1e: Many candidates produced a well-argued discussion of both options together with a valid, supported decision. The most common error from many candidates was to state that dividends would have to be paid without noting the discretionary nature of such payments.
notes.2i: Most candidates were able to state three possible causes of depreciation.
notes.2ii: Preparation of the provision for depreciation account and the disposal account were not satisfactory. Firstly, candidates should be aware that T-accounts MUST include dates and details – they are incomplete without them. Many candidates did not demonstrate knowledge of basic bookkeeping, though well-prepared candidates were able to produce totally correct accounts.
notes.3a: Most candidates were able to offer three advantages to a business of preparing control accounts, though development of the advantages was often either missing or very vague.
notes.3b: Preparation of the sales ledger control account was generally very well done by a large number of candidates. The most common error related to the narrative entered in the details column. Many candidates stated ‘receipts from trade receivables’ whereas the correct narrative is ‘bank’. Less well-prepared candidates included items such as cash sales in the control account.
notes.4a: Very few candidates were able to explain the difference between overhead allocation and overhead apportionment. Most simply stated that one allocated and one apportioned.
notes.4i: The meaning of a production department resulted in some excellent responses though some candidates simply responded that it involved making a product without indicating that it is directly involved in the production.
notes.4ii: Many answers were too vague, missing the point that service departments are indirectly involved in production.
notes.4c: Completion of the table to apportion the overheads was generally well done by most candidates.
notes.4d: Calculation of the overhead absorption rate was well done by most candidates though a number of them did not state the basis, that is, per labour hour or per machine hour.
notes.4e: Few candidates were able to explain the reason for the re-apportionment of service department costs. Some candidates did not recognise that the purpose was to ensure that all costs are then recovered in the sale of products being the main issue.
notes.4f: The question on limitations of absorption costing was not well answered. The fact that it is not useful for short-term decision making was often the only valid response.
notes.4g: Calculation of the price to quote for the special order was generally answered reasonably well. A majority of candidates were unable to correctly apply the correct mark-up.
notes.4h: The final task, to advise whether or not to accept the customer’s offer, was well answered with most candidates sating the effect on profit and the effect on other existing customers. ACCOUNTING
notes.key_messages: Read the questions carefully. Identify what you are being asked and eliminate any data which is not relevant.
